claims.text: The onset and progression of phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are governed by a thermally induced reduction in a surface energy barrier.
Reduction of the surface energy barrier triggers surface atomic rearrangements.
Surface atomic rearrangements nucleate premelting at the nanoparticle surface.
Slight oxidation or ligand passivation can increase the relevant surface energy barrier.
In situ TEM is suitable for monitoring nanoscale kinetic processes during heating.
Restricting the comparison to particles of approximately 5–10 nm helps isolate surface-related effects.
Surface rearrangement produces a disordered or partially amorphous surface layer before bulk melting.
Surface atomic rearrangements result in a reduced energetic barrier.
At a critical temperature, thermal activation increases the mobility of surface atoms.
The surface-initiated melting front propagates inward as temperature increases.
Particles with artificially increased surface barriers undergo premelting-related changes at higher temperatures.
Unmodified particles will exhibit increased surface roughness or amorphous behavior during heating.
The surface changes in unmodified particles will coincide with an endothermic DSC event.
Passivated particles will show delayed surface transformations and a higher transition-onset temperature than unmodified particles.
As-synthesized surfaces have a lower relevant surface energy barrier than the proposed modified surfaces.
The proposed mechanism is limited to similarly sized FeNiCrCoCu particles under controlled inert atmospheres and defined heating rates.
Bulk defects or impurities may also contribute to the observed transition.
A lack of a statistically significant onset-temperature shift or morphological difference between modified and native particles would falsify surface-barrier reduction as the dominant mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and mechanism place reduction of the surface energy barrier before and as the cause of atomic rearrangement, whereas the structural mediator says atomic rearrangements result in the reduced barrier. This reverses the proposed causal order and makes the mechanism partly circular.
